evidence.summary: 44 of 51 cases passed with worst absolute error 1.06e-6, orders of magnitude inside the 0.01+0.0002|target| tolerance. The 7 reported failures are probe bugs, not kernel defects: my "zero" mode produced route weights whose row sums exceeded 1, which validate_inputs correctly rejected ("route weights sum exceeds one"). Zero-weight rows were still covered by the passing "allzero" mode (all rows zero), and legal edge layouts all passed: expert receiving zero routes, all tokens sharing the same expert pair, Q=1 all-to-one-expert, extreme +/-0.5 FP16 values, shapes from 1x1x1 to 129x129x129, E up to 8, Q up to 4.

rationale: The kernel uses a custom argsort/padding routing preparation and a grouped Triton schedule; an off-by-one or swizzle bug could drop routes or duplicate tiles, and fp16 tl.dot with fp32 accumulation should otherwise stay well within tolerance.

scope_evidence.summary: Every output must satisfy abs(actual - target) <= 0.01 + 0.0002*abs(target); correctness covers every legal shape, value and routing layout (M,K,N in [1,129], E in [1,8], Q in [1,min(4,E)], zero weights and all-zero rows legal, an expert may receive zero or up to M routes).

scope_rationale: The contract requires the tolerance bound for every legal shape/value/routing layout; a missed route or out-of-tolerance output on a contract-admitted input violates it.
statement: run() deviates from the FP64 reference beyond the contract tolerance (0.01 + 0.0002*|target|) or drops/duplicates routes for some legal input configuration (shapes M,K,N in [1,129], E in [1,8], Q in [1,min(4,E)], skewed routing, zero weights).
